statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2018-1000021: Git prints the progress and error messages a remote server sends over the sideband (the "remote:" lines) to the user's terminal without removing control characters, so a malicious server, or an attacker who can modify the traffic, can send ANSI escape sequences that alter the terminal's state or hide output; the report describes the impact: http://www.batterystapl.es/2018/01/security-implications-of-ansi-escape.html . The Debian tracker lists git as unfixed in trixie with urgency unimportant ("Terminal emulators need to perform proper escaping"): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2018-1000021 . That is a decision not to ship a fix, not evidence that the code is absent. Upstream Git 2.55.0 now masks control characters in sideband messages by default, except ANSI color sequences, as its release notes say: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.55.0/Documentation/RelNotes/2.55.0.adoc . The masking starts with commit https://github.com/git/git/commit/04949538203ba7aeb298a607280715d4f26dbe0a , which addresses this escape-sequence injection but does not name the CVE. This owner ships Git 2.47.3, whose sideband.c passes control characters in remote messages through unchanged: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.47.3/sideband.c . DHI does not backport the masking. We checked every ELF program in the git package of the two builds in the DHI Debian repository, on amd64 and arm64: none contains the string "sideband.allowcontrolcharacters", the configuration key the masking series reads, while every one contains the existing "color.remote" key. The same search finds that key in /usr/bin/git from Alpine's Git 2.56.1-r0 package. Every published build of this owner is therefore affected.
